grammar.label: which referring back to a whole clause
grammar.form: , which + verb — after a complete clause
grammar.meaning: comments on the entire preceding statement, not on one noun

explanation.en: 'They cancelled the meeting, which surprised everyone' — 'which' refers to the cancelling, not to the meeting. This use always needs a comma, and 'what' can never replace 'which' here.
explanation.uz: 'They cancelled the meeting, which surprised everyone' — 'which' bekor qilinganiga ishora qiladi, yig'ilishga emas. Bunda vergul shart va 'what' ishlatilmaydi.

grammar.positive_example: The train was an hour late, which meant we missed the opening.
grammar.negative_example: The train was an hour late, what meant we missed the opening.

l1_notes.uz: Rus tilidagi 'что' ta'sirida 'what' ishlatiladi; ingliz tilida bu o'rinda faqat 'which' to'g'ri.

grammar.label: quantifier + of which / of whom
grammar.form: some / many / most / none / both / all + of which / of whom
grammar.meaning: says how much of a previously mentioned group is involved

explanation.en: 'We interviewed forty staff, most of whom had never been asked before.' Use 'of whom' for people and 'of which' for things. The form is never 'of who', and this pattern belongs to writing — speech prefers 'and most of them'.
explanation.uz: 'We interviewed forty staff, most of whom had never been asked before.' Odamlar uchun 'of whom', narsalar uchun 'of which'. 'of who' shakli yo'q; bu qurilma yozma uslubga xos.

grammar.positive_example: The report lists sixty cases, none of which was investigated.
grammar.negative_example: The report lists sixty cases, none of them was investigated.

l1_notes.uz: 'whom' shakli o'zbek tilida muqobilsiz; uni predlogdan keyingi majburiy shakl sifatida yodlash kerak.
